approve_action.description: Approve an action a run holds (run_id and item_id from list_actions): it is published to the workflow's mission control connections as an instruction to carry out (a swap can cancel a booked pass) and cannot be rejected afterwards. The approval stands for the same action on the workflow's later runs. Needs the Operator + Act plan (403 plan_required below it), the act:approve scope and a live key.

create_scenario.description: Create a scenario overlay: antennas taken down, and extra attenuation in dB per antenna. Returns a scenario_id for run_workflow. Requires the config:write scope.

get_fleet.description: The fleet as declared and as observed, from GET /topology: config is the latest network config ({version, document}; null when there is none or the key lacks config:read), and state is the newest value of each field per ground antenna and satellite reported within freshness_seconds (default 300, at most 3600). An empty state means nothing has reported in the window. Requires the topology:read scope.

get_network_config.description: The caller's network config: its ground stations with their antennas, and its satellites with their radios. version picks an older one; the latest otherwise. Contact predictions run over the antennas and satellites named here.

get_passes.description: Every pass of the network config's satellites over its antennas between from and to, from the live orbit catalog and each antenna's elevation mask, sampled every step_s seconds. Each pass carries the pass_id a run's item for it carries. satellite_id and antenna_id narrow it. Below the Operator plan it covers at most 2 satellites of the caller's own; the demo fleet's are free. Every time carries a UTC offset. Requires the topology:read scope.

get_predictions.description: Forecasts for named entities from Constellation's models; the ids go in link_ids whatever the family. The default family, snr, returns signal-to-noise forecasts in dB as a point value (snr_db_p50) per link and horizon; optical links (3000 GHz or more) return rx_power_dbm_p50, received power in dBm under clear sky; a link id is a ground antenna id from the caller's network config (see get_topology). To ask snr by instant, pass at (a future UTC instant) with a satellite_id, a ground_station_id or ground_antenna_id, or both sides, and no link_ids: each link up at that instant comes back with its snr_db_p50, named by ground_station_id, ground_antenna_id and satellite_id. Up to 100 ids per call, of which at most 25 without a stored forecast are computed in one call. Entities that cannot be answered are listed in entity_errors with a code: no_telemetry or insufficient_telemetry means the input telemetry is missing or stale, and prediction_unavailable means the id was declined for now (the message says why, e.g. a per-call limit or a busy fill) and a later retry can answer it. Retry only the declined ids, after a short pause, not in a loop. weather-attenuation takes no link_ids: it prices the slant-path attenuation in dB of the links of the caller's network config at one future instant, at, for a ground_station_id, a satellite_id or both. With both, every antenna at the station is priced against the satellite; with one, only the links in view and on a common band. Each item names its ground_station_id, ground_antenna_id and satellite_id. Requires the predictions:read scope.

as_of_utc.description: Return the prediction that existed at this past instant.

at.description: weather-attenuation (required there), or snr: the future UTC instant to forecast the links at.

ground_antenna_id.description: snr with at: ground antenna ids from the network config; not with ground_station_id.

ground_station_id.description: weather-attenuation, or snr with at: a ground station id from the network config.

horizon_minutes.description: Forecast horizon. Omit to let the model choose.

link_ids.description: Ids to forecast: ground antenna ids for snr. Not taken by weather-attenuation.

model_family.description: snr (default) for link SNR, or weather-attenuation for a link's attenuation at one instant.

satellite_id.description: weather-attenuation, or snr with at: a satellite id from the network config.

get_run.description: A run by run_id, or a workflow's newest finished run by its slug (workflow; 409 no_finished_run until one finishes). Answers the run's status (queued, running, done, failed or cancelled) and, when done, its items: each names its entity (type pass, link or antenna, with its ids) and target_at, with value p10/p50/p90 and the explain ledger naming each lane's value and source. A held action on an item carries its action_status. A run can hold thousands of items, so read them in pages: page_records items from page (next_page while more are left), and narrow with satellite_id, antenna_id, station_id or pass_id. Not counted as a prediction. Requires the predictions:read scope and a live key.

get_telemetry_v2.description: Link telemetry written with send_telemetry_v2 between start and end, one record per time and id set, oldest first. Set interval and agg to aggregate numeric fields into windows; a raw read spans at most an hour. Requires the topology:read scope.

get_topology.description: The newest value of each field per ground antenna and satellite reported within freshness_seconds (default 300, at most 3600). An empty list means nothing has reported in the window. Requires the topology:read scope.

get_usage.description: The caller's account: plan and this month's usage per unit (predictions, chat turns, telemetry points) and when the month resets. Usage is counted, never capped.

list_actions.description: The actions a workflow's current run holds for approval (a swap to book, a reroute), each pending, approved, rejected or expired, with the deadline to decide by, its action_id and, once decided, its decision_id. A run holds an action when its workflow has a policy step in approve mode. Requires the predictions:read scope and a live key.

list_workflows.description: The caller's saved workflows (the Platform's Automations tab), the latest version of each, as a name and a node graph. With templates true, the read-only templates instead (pass-yield, antenna-capacity, modcod-plan, rain-fade-swap, audit-ledger, and rfi-watch, marked available false where no rfi model is served), and lanes: each lane with whether a run prices it here and, where not, why; copy a template by saving its graph with put_workflow under your own slug. Requires the config:read, config:write or workflows:write scope and a live key.

load_demo_fleet.description: Load a ready-made demo fleet into the caller's account, so the other tools have data: 5 ground stations with 6 antennas and 5 sun-synchronous Earth observation satellites on X and Ka band (ids norad-<NORAD id>) in the network config, and the link telemetry of every pass in the last two hours at a 30 second cadence (es_n0_db, elevation_deg, range_m and frequency_ghz), from the live orbit catalog. The call merges the demo stations, antennas and satellites, with their RF terms, into the caller's network config with PATCH /topology/config, unless the config already holds a demo id (as on a reload), so no tenant entity is overwritten. The telemetry names the demo ids, so on a fresh account a key without config:write fails the call, and the error says so. The SNR is synthetic: a planted offset per link (a known answer for calibration, not a measured loss), plus a slow wander and noise. Each link's es_n0_db also drops by the rain attenuation its ground station stored for the last 30 minutes, scaled to the link's elevation. Older records are not faded, nor is a link with no stored terms; rain_note counts those links, or says the stored terms could not be read. The data ends at the present and does not advance; calling again rewrites the same points, so it is safe to repeat. SNR forecasts need telemetry from the last minute, so call load_demo_fleet again right before get_predictions. Requires the telemetry:write scope.

patch_network_config.description: Merge a JSON merge patch into the caller's network config and store it as a new version: add or change ground stations, antennas and satellites. A satellite takes a norad_id or a tle. A satellite with catalog {norad_id} or a station with catalog {station_id} (from search_catalog) is filled from the catalog where the document leaves fields out; the document's own fields win and radio values are never filled. Requires the config:write scope.

put_workflow.description: Save a workflow under a slug as a new version: a name and a graph of nodes ({id, kind, ref, params, position}) and edges ({id, from: {node, port}, to: {node, port}}). Kinds: input (passes or links: step_s, satellite_ids, antenna_ids), lane (snr, weather; demand, rfi and ssa run only once a model serves them), transform (sinr, capacity, success, expected_gb, sum_by, modcod_schedule, swap, ledger, lock_loss), condition (threshold: column, quantile, op, value; ports true and false), output (predictions, exactly one; feed; destination). Start from a template's graph (list_workflows with templates true). A graph with issues is refused with each one. Requires the workflows:write or config:write scope and a live key.

reject_action.description: Reject an action a run holds (run_id and item_id from list_actions): nothing is published, it cannot be decided again, and later runs hold the same action back as rejected. Requires the act:approve scope and a live key.

run_workflow.description: Start a run of a saved workflow over a UTC window (from and to) or at one time (at), optionally against a scenario_id. Returns a run_id for get_run; the run queues and runs in the background. Every time carries a UTC offset. deliver false is a test run: it prices and stores its items and sends nothing, and a run against a scenario is always one. A run that delivers needs the Operator plan or above; a plan without it is refused with 403 plan_required. A run computes at most 4,000,000 link steps (links times steps): more is refused with 422 too_many_link_steps and a suggested_step_s that fits. Requires the workflows:write scope and a live key.

search_catalog.description: Search the public asset catalog to build a fleet from it: kind satellites (by NORAD id, with downlink bands) or stations (ground stations, with receive bands, coordinates and antenna counts). q matches name, id or operator; operator, fleet and band (S, X, Ka) filter; near (lat,lon) with within_km finds stations nearest first. Pages of limit (default 50) with next_cursor. Add a pick with patch_network_config: a satellite {"catalog": {"norad_id": N}}, a station {"catalog": {"station_id": id}}. Requires the topology:read scope.

send_telemetry_v2.description: Write link telemetry keyed by the caller's network config: up to 1,000 records per call. Each record names a ground_station_id, one of its ground_antenna_ids and a satellite_id, as the network config has them. Antenna fields: azimuth_deg, elevation_deg, tracking_error_az_deg, tracking_error_el_deg, track_mode, range_m, range_rate_m_s. Carrier fields: carrier_locked, subcarrier_locked, symbol_locked, frame_locked, c_n0_dbhz, es_n0_db, rx_power_dbm, frequency_ghz, carrier_offset_hz, frames_delivered, frames_good, uplink_status, modcod, tx_power_dbm, ber, per, system_noise_temp_k, noise_power_dbm, noise_diode_on. The records that pass are written; rejected_indices and rejections name the rest with each index, field and reason. The call is an error only when no record passes, or a record does not match the schema. Requires the telemetry:write scope.
